title: Neither harmonic benchmarks nor a default SSCHA cross-check certifies a foundation machine-learning interatomic potential for finite-temperature dynamic stability
content: Foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are benchmarked mainly on harmonic phonons, yet cubic perovskites, bcc metals and fluorites are harmonically unstable and thermally stabilised. We test five, as shipped, using 20 systems. Harmonically, MatterSim and SevenNet-0 score 19/19; MACE-MP-0 and CHGNet flatten the bcc Zr and Hf instabilities. A single-mode quantum self-consistent harmonic approximation (SCHA) screen shows that harmonic correctness does not certify the finite-temperature calls made with a model: at 300 K, 17 harmonically correct units are mis-called against 4 the other way (7–24 under other conventions), which is insignificant when system-clustered (p = 0.15). PBE on the screen's coordinates corrects eight (BaTiO3 and KNbO3), but PBE at its own lattice, which is 0.3–0.8% smaller, errs alike on the modes profiled, and the pre-registered fine-tuning toward PBE corrected neither. Converged, replicated stochastic SCHA (SSCHA), by its default symmetric-point Hessian, calls 27 of 77 label-unstable non-bcc units stable (seven unresolved), all of which are oxide perovskites (23/73 without four size-untested SrTiO3 units); on the same energies, the screen, which moves one mode with the rest frozen, finds a lower displaced minimum in 15 of them. A pre-registered multi-mode SSCHA test of one (BaTiO3, MACE-MP-0, 100 K) puts the free energy at the screen's minimum, a zone-boundary M-point displacement, 46 ± 2 meV per 40 atoms above the cubic point: on this unit, the two methods differ through mode coupling, not through where the curvature is read. Fluorite false-stables vanish. On ferroelectric perovskites at T ≤ 300 K, the screen recovers 14/22 [0.43, 0.80], mostly through zone-boundary modes, against 4/22 [0.07, 0.39] for converged SSCHA (paired, system-clustered p = 0.5). Ensemble vote splits flag consensus errors (AUC 0.76 [0.59, 0.93]), not robustly (0.63 without ORB-v2); force-level spread does not do the same because about half or more of the force error on thermally sampled configurations is common to all five models.
